title.value: Probabilistic Surrogate Networks for Simulators with Unbounded Randomness
title.justification: The chosen title captures the paper's main focus on developing surrogate networks for simulators characterized by unbounded randomness.
title.quote: We present a framework for automatically structuring and training fast, approximate, deep neural surrogates of stochastic simulators.

extractions.description: The paper introduces a framework for building deep neural network surrogates for stochastic simulators where the number of random variables can be unbounded. It discusses the efficiency and speed of these surrogates in modeling complex stochastic programs and enabling faster simulations and Bayesian inference. The paper also illustrates the application of the framework through stochastic control flows, program synthesis, and composite materials process simulation.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the development of a deep learning framework for surrogate modeling in simulators. Although there is mention of an application in composite materials, the core theme is not centered on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Using an illustrative yet non-trivial example we show our surrogates’ ability to accurately model a probabilistic program...

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as its primary objective. It primarily addresses computational advancements in surrogate modeling.
primary_category.quote: Our framework further enables an automatic replacement of the reference simulator with the surrogate when undertaking amortized inference.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper briefly touches on applications relevant to process simulation in composite materials, which can have implications for manufacturing processes affecting environmental outcomes, though it's not the core theme.
secondary_categories.quote: We show how to use inference to estimate the temperature of the part in regions that cannot be accessed non-invasively. Such results are critical for determining whether the part is safe or not.

primary_sub_category.justification: The main content does not directly align with any specific sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: The fidelity and speed of our surrogates allow for both faster stochastic simulation and accurate and substantially faster posterior inference.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper implies potential benefits to industrial processes by using surrogate modeling for temperature estimation during composite material curing, which can enhance process optimization.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Using probabilistic programming and our PSNs, we seek to infer the internal state of the material conditioned on realistically observable quantities.

applications.justification: The paper applies its framework to simulate the curing process in composite materials, which can indirectly contribute to more sustainable manufacturing practices.
applications.quote: In this experiment we train a surrogate model for a commercial heat-transfer finite element analysis simulator, depicted in Fig. 3, that is used to model the cure cycle for composite aircraft parts.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our main contribution is to develop a construction in which the surrogates allow for the description of a dynamically growing number of random variables, while maintaining consistency of the assigned probability measure as new variables are encountered.
